source.author: stat
source.text: Primus sudor equis, dic inclyta, Phoebe, regentum nomina, dic ipsos; neque enim generosior umquam alipedum collata acies, ceu praepete cursu confligant densae volucres aut litore in uno Aeolus insanis statuat certamina ventis.
source.text_original: Primus sudor equis, dic inclyta, Phoebe, regentum / nomina, dic ipsos; neque enim generosior umquam / alipedum collata acies, ceu praepete cursu / confligant densae volucres aut litore in uno / Aeolus insanis statuat certamina ventis.
source.text_english: First comes the sweat for the horses. Tell, glorious Phoebus, the names of the chariot-riders; tell them themselves, for never was there a nobler array of wing-footed steeds, as though thick ranks of birds were to contend in a swift flight, or Aeolus were to set the winds themselves in wild contest upon one shore.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: omne dei rapidis nemus ingemit alis, strata Ceres, motusque niger sub praepete pontus.
reuse.text_original: omne dei rapidis nemus ingemit alis, / strata Ceres, motusque niger sub praepete pontus.
reuse.text_english: All the grove of the god groans with rapid wings; Ceres is laid low, and the black sea is stirred beneath the swift bird.
